mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES continues to rise from its recent trough, commuting-linked foot traffic will rebuild retail visits with a short lag, pushing RETAIL_REC above its prior 4-week mean over the next month.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -23.4 to -12.4 while TRANSIT remained elevated at roughly -19 to -21
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT rise or stay stable for four weeks but RETAIL_REC does not exceed its prior 4-week average, the commuting-to-retail mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT falls sharply below its recent level, discretionary trips to shopping and dining locations are immediately compressed, lowering RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 3 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT stayed negative and moved from -20.1 to -18.6 in the latest week after prior weakness
failure_condition: If a week-on-week TRANSIT drop larger than 3 points is followed by flat or higher RETAIL_REC in the next week, the transit-shock channel fails.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT signals renewed mobility restraint or workplace avoidance, and retail mobility will weaken over the next two weeks because fewer commuters create fewer incidental retail stops.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES stays below -10 while TRANSIT stays below -15 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES has been at or below -14 except the latest week at -12.4; TRANSIT has remained near -19 to -23
failure_condition: If both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain below the stated thresholds for two weeks and RETAIL_REC still rises over the following two weeks, the restraint mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Higher PARKS mobility captures weather and leisure conditions that draw discretionary activity away from indoor retail; if PARKS rebounds from its recent trough, RETAIL_REC will soften over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 5 points from its recent weekly low
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from -6.9 to -20.1 before partially recovering to -13.9
failure_condition: If PARKS rebounds by at least 5 points from its recent low and RETAIL_REC does not decline relative to the prior 4-week mean, the leisure-substitution hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent gains in GROCERY_PHARM indicate routine local errands are strengthening, and those trips spill over into nearby retail visits; the effect appears within two weeks and lifts RETAIL_REC.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM has been positive in three of four weeks while RESIDENTIAL remains above baseline around 7-9
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM stays above baseline while RESIDENTIAL remains elevated but RETAIL_REC does not improve within two weeks, the local-errands spillover mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL remains elevated while WORKPLACES stay depressed, consumers substitute toward local retail near home rather than commute-based shopping, causing RETAIL_REC to rise over the next month.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stays above 5 while WORKPLACES stays below -10
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL is persistently positive near 7-9 while WORKPLACES is still negative near -12 to -23
failure_condition: If the specified home-based pattern persists but RETAIL_REC remains flat or declines over four weeks, the local-substitution hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A crossover from declining to improving TRANSIT mobility marks easing access conditions; once TRANSIT rises for two consecutive weeks, retail mobility should stop falling and turn upward within four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT increases for two consecutive weeks after being below -18
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -22.6 to -18.6 across the snapshot and is the weakest access channel among the place categories
failure_condition: If TRANSIT posts two consecutive weekly gains after remaining below -18 and RETAIL_REC still fails to rise over the next four weeks, the access-recovery hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS combined with stable GROCERY_PHARM indicates broader willingness to leave home for discretionary activities, and that sentiment should lift RETAIL_REC after a one-week lag.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises week-on-week while GROCERY_PHARM stays non-negative
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS recovered from -20.1 to -13.9 while GROCERY_PHARM stayed at or above baseline in the latest weeks
failure_condition: If PARKS rises while GROCERY_PHARM remains at or above baseline but RETAIL_REC does not improve in the next week, the discretionary-confidence signal is rejected.
